record.title: Phishing Wave Incident Retro
record.summary: The team reviewed the phishing incident from last week. The first reported click occurred at 09:14, with containment actions starting at 09:52, resulting in a 38-minute response time. Marcus identified a process gap where 11 minutes were lost waiting for him to exit a meeting, highlighting the need for an escalation process that does not rely on a single person. Regarding scope, 214 users received the email, 9 clicked, and 3 entered credentials. All three users reset their credentials within an hour, and no successful logins from attacker infrastructure were observed. The credential entries occurred on a fake ADFS page. Rio noted that phishing-resistant MFA is not enforced for the finance group due to an ERP migration exemption that has been in place for two years. Since the ERP vendor now supports FIDO keys as of their March release, removing the exemption is feasible via a config change and comms plan. Rio will stage the removal, starting with a pilot of five finance users next week. Priya confirmed that phishing domains have been added to the blocklist feed and a takedown request was sent to the registrar an hour ago. Detection improvements were discussed; the fake page was live for six hours before reporting. Rio suggested adding a canary token to the login footer template to catch clones earlier. Marcus noted that users received no acknowledgment for their reports, leading to re-reports, and suggested an auto-ack feature. Dana assigned the escalation runbook to Marcus, MFA exemption removal to Rio, and placed canary tokens and auto-ack into the backlog.
